subject: Engagement stack consolidation after acquisition — vendor shortlist & migration sequencing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Engagement stack consolidation after acquisition — initial ask

Team —

Quick context: Acme (the company we closed last month) runs Salesloft + a small Salesforce instance. We currently use Outreach + HubSpot and the overlap is creating duplicate workflows, extra seats, and support overhead. Procurement would like a recommendation by EoQ on whether to consolidate (and if so, to which vendor), or run a longer coexistence plan.

Ask: can the sales systems squad put together a 2-week vendor discovery focused on: seat counts, integration gaps (SFDC <> engagement), SSO/SAML implications, SOC2/security, estimated migration lift (data + sequences), and a preliminary cost delta? Attached is a quick export of current seat counts and the Acme inventory.

Proposed owners: Marissa (product ops) to lead the discovery, Hannah to own vendor selection recommendations, Ben for contract/commercial comparisons, Monica (CS) for migration impact on customers.

Can we meet 10/27 to align on scope?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, GTM Platforms
Redwood Inference

Attachments: current_seat_counts.csv

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@outreach.io>, AJ Turner <aj.turner@salesloft.com>, ClearBridge Advisors <engage@clearbridgeadvisors.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Engagement stack consolidation after acquisition — initial ask

On Sun, Oct 25, 2026 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick context: Acme (the company we closed last month) runs Salesloft + a small Salesforce instance. We currently use Outreach + HubSpot and the overlap is creating duplicate workflows, extra seats, and support overhead. Procurement would like a recommendation by EoQ on whether to consolidate (and if so, to which vendor), or run a longer coexistence plan.
> 
> Ask: can the sales systems squad put together a 2-week vendor discovery focused on: seat counts, integration gaps (SFDC <> engagement), SSO/SAML implications, SOC2/security, estimated migration lift (data + sequences), and a preliminary cost delta? Attached is a quick export of current seat counts and the Acme inventory.
> 
> Proposed owners: Marissa (product ops) to lead the discovery, Hannah to own vendor selection recommendations, Ben for contract/commercial comparisons, Monica (CS) for migration impact on customers.
> 
> Can we meet 10/27 to align on scope?

Agree with the scope — I'm looping in two vendor contacts and the consultancy we used for the SQL region migration last year (ClearBridge) so they can advise on sequencing and data migration risk. High-level constraints to bake into vendor asks:
- Must support bi-directional SFDC sync for activities and custom objects (we can't lose activity attribution)
- SSO via Okta (SAML) is required for both Redwood and Acme groups
- SOC2 + pen-test report access during procurement review
- Prefer vendors that can offer migration tooling or credits for seat conversions

Priya / AJ — can you provide: a one-page implementation checklist, typical pilot duration, reference for a 100–250 seat migration, and any commercial transition programs (credits or term extensions) you offer for consolidation deals?

Marissa — 10/27 11:00am PT works for me to kick off. I'll draft the RFP template and share before the call.

— Hannah
Director, Sales Systems
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@outreach.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Outreach: quick implementation checklist + pilot offer

Thanks for the invite and context, Hannah —

High level from Outreach: we do several 100–300 seat consolidations per year. Attached is a short proposal and an implementation checklist that covers SFDC mapping, sequence import, activity mapping, and a recommended pilot cadence. Highlights:
- Pilot: 2–4 weeks (scope: 10–20 seats, key sequences, and SFDC mapping verification)
- Typical full migration: 6–10 weeks with dedicated migration engineering support (depends on sequence complexity)
- Security: SOC2 Type II available for review; we can share a redacted pen-test summary under NDA
- Commercial: we can offer a 30% prorated seat credit for overlapping licenses and one month of complimentary onboarding support for migrations agreed by EoQ

I'll follow up with a technical lead for a 1 hr deep dive next week.

Attachments: Outreach_proposal_v1.pdf

Best,
Priya Shah
Enterprise Account Executive — Outreach

From: AJ Turner <aj.turner@salesloft.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Salesloft migration support and commercial alternative

Hannah / team —

Appreciate the heads-up. We support migrations from Outreach and have a partnership playbook specifically for acquisitions. Quick bullets:
- Migration outline attached (mapping, export/import of cadences, activity reconciliation). We can provide tooling to bulk convert cadence steps into Salesloft sequences.
- Pilot: 3 weeks to validate hooks and analytics events in SFDC.
- Commercial: for customers moving consolidation to Salesloft we have a limited-time promotion: up to 25% seat credit + first three months at a reduced rate for transferred seats.
- References: we can share two customers with 150+ seat consolidations on request.

Attachments: Salesloft-migration-outline.docx

Happy to set a technical call with our migration engineering team; proposed 11/16 11am PT.

— AJ Turner
Partner Sales — Salesloft

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Engagement stack consolidation after acquisition — vendor shortlist & migration sequencing

Thanks for the proposals, Priya and AJ — useful detail. Quick internal summary and recommended next steps:

Summary of vendor asks received:
- Outreach: shorter pilot (2–4 weeks), 30% prorated credit, SOC2 under NDA, 6–10 week finish estimate
- Salesloft: 3 week pilot, up to 25% credit + promotional pricing, tooling support for cadence conversion

Decision drivers we should weigh: total TCO (subscription + migration lift), integration fidelity with our Salesforce custom objects, migration risk to active sequences, and procurement terms (termination windows & data extraction costs).

Recommended immediate plan (next 30 days):
1) Procurement (Ben) to produce a two-column commercial comparison (list pricing, prorated credit mechanics, typical SOW fees) — target 11/19
2) ClearBridge (Monica to coordinate intro) to run a migration-risk quick-scan on a representative set of 20 sequences — target 11/23
3) Technical deep dives with both vendors (engineering + migration lead) — target week of 11/16; I'll confirm times with vendor reps
4) Prepare a short exec memo summarizing recommended vendor + expected delta vs do-nothing by 11/30 so Finance can evaluate.

Marissa — can you confirm the 20 sequence sample and give Ben access to the seat-count sheet? I'll add the RFP template to the shared drive (link below).

Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/placeholder-migration-plan

Hannah
Director, Sales Systems
Redwood Inference
